title: Automatically select light/dark theme variant
body:
<!--
Your enhancement may already be reported!
Please search on the issue tracker before creating a new issue.
If this is an idea for a feature, please open an "Idea" Discussion instead.
-->

Query the terminal background color and choose a dark or light variant of a theme accordingly. This would be very convenient for people who switch between light/dark terminal themes.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Well ok technically not quite the same, I'll leave it open for opinions

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: This is probably simpler/smaller to add than #2158 (we can query the host terminal for the current background color, right?) but would be less powerful - there wouldn't be any automatic switching when the OS switches between day/night unless we were constantly polling. We could check again on config reload (so you would script something to send all Helix instances the `USR1` signal when the OS switches) but if you're doing that then it isn't much more complicated to also swap configs in the external script between light and dark themes. IMO it is still better to accomplish this outside of Helix.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> we can query the host terminal for the current background color, right?

Yes, `neovim` does that.

> swap configs in the external script

I do this with `kitty`, but only because I can include config files from my main configuration. Keeping two copies of the same config is not ideal.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: What some people do instead is have `theme = "theme.toml` and then just swap the files (rather than editing the config) for the theme they want to use, and then reload the config.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Bat [just merged in auto theme switching based on terminal color](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/2896) using a custom library called [terminal colorsaurus](https://github.com/bash/terminal-colorsaurus), which is written in rust and is published as a crate. Delta also uses that library [since version 0.17, March of this year](https://github.com/dandavison/delta/pull/1615)

With the next release it even seems to be supporting windows with the terminal app. 

So MacOS, Linux and Windows are supported with most to pretty much all terminal emulators working, [see here](https://github.com/bash/terminal-colorsaurus/blob/main/doc/terminal-survey.md).

I think this issue should be revisited

_Originally posted by @participant12 in https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/discussions/10281#discussioncomment-11246639_

This is great, I didn't know this was possible. Is this documented anywhere or it that some kind of convention? Writing a script now that toggles themes for all my apps.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
This work: 

`kill -USR1 $(ps -C hx -o pid | tail -n1)`


eq:

`sed -i 's/theme\s*=\s*".*"/theme = "cyan_light"/' ~/.config/helix/config.toml && kill -USR1 $(ps -C hx -o pid | tail -n1)`

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I'd really love for this to be enabled in Helix as well. For now I used systemd user unit files to accomplish this. It watches for changes to the COSMIC theme and updates the Helix theme accordingly. Wrote about it in more detail at https://matthewsanabria.dev/posts/helix-theme-syncing-with-cosmic/.

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/helix-theme-sync.service
[Unit]
Description=Sync Helix theme with COSMIC theme

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env nu %h/bin/helix-theme-sync.nu

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/helix-theme-sync.path
[Unit]
Description=Watch COSMIC theme changes

[Path]
PathModified=%h/.config/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicTheme.Mode/v1/is_dark

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
My **edit.fish** (edit function) for Fish Shell
```fish
function edit
    if status is-interactive
        switch (uname)
            case Darwin
                if type -q defaults
                    # Check if macOS is in dark mode
                    defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle >/dev/null 2>&1
                    if test $status -eq 0
                        hx -c ~/.config/helix/config-dark.toml $argv
                    else
                        hx -c ~/.config/helix/config-light.toml $argv
                    end
                end
            case Linux
                # Modern Linux desktops (GNOME, MATE, XFCE, etc.)
                if type -q gsettings
                    # Get standard freedesktop color-scheme preference
                    set -l mode (gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme 2>/dev/null)
                    if test "$mode" = "'prefer-dark'"
                        hx -c ~/.config/helix/config-dark.toml $argv
                    else
                        hx -c ~/.config/helix/config-light.toml $argv
                    end
                end

            case '*'
                # Fallback fallback theme for unsupported OS (like Windows WSL)
                hx $argv
        end
    else
        hx $argv
    end
end
